reviews.text:
Male cat, 7 years old, 4.7kg
He only likes dry food, and was constipated, hadn't pooped for two days, and was crying out in the litter box. I frantically called first thing in the morning, and they told me when they had an opening and came to see him right away. The response was quick, and the doctor and nurses were kind and spoke to me gently. This is a trustworthy animal hospital.

My dog ​​seemed to love the kind doctor and receptionist, and was always wagging his tail happily on the examination table. Many hospitals take dogs to the back, but I was glad to see them treating my dog ​​while speaking to him gently. We have moved and can no longer go there, but we are very grateful for the care we received there for five years, from when he was a puppy.
This is the worst. Please give my child back. I developed PTSD from the shock, and my heart aches and I can't escape the pain every day. I wish this hospital would go out of business.
This is a truly wonderful hospital that treats both pet owners and animals with sincerity.

I always come here for my toy poodle, Azuki's, skin care. The doctor always makes accurate decisions when prescribing medication, and the bright red skin that was there before always fades and clears up after two weeks. Above all, I'm happy to see Azuki's smile disappear after the itch is gone. Not only does he examine her skin, he also examines and trims her nails. Her ears are red, so he prescribes a topical ointment. He's given this before, and the redness clears up within a week! They also sell pills that dogs who don't like medicine can take, which is very helpful. It's clear that the female staff love dogs, and they're always so affectionate. I would recommend Taro Animal Hospital to anyone, and the doctor and staff are always so kind and helpful, whether they're dealing with skin problems or anything else.
They are kind doctors and nurses.

I didn't want to waste my dog's vaccinations, so I came in for an antibody test, but I was shocked by how bad the blood draw was.
In the end, they couldn't get blood from one leg and had to draw from both, but they couldn't seem to find a vein and kept poking the dog over and over again, which was unbearable to watch.
The doctors at the two other hospitals I usually go to draw blood quickly and easily, so I was really surprised at how different it was.
